scenario.title: Source maintenance and administrative contract tools
situations: A Yoke contributor renders agents/packets or checks generated artifacts.
A source operator rehearses convergence, handles a cutover or debugs a contract.
An integration supplies invalid timestamps or needs exact function/schema semantics.
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
questions: Catalogued as an audience boundary, not a claim every command in a mixed namespace is admin-only.
Current source/public corpus and installed help may represent different revisions; reconcile before publication.

lessons.title: Route source work out of the ordinary product journey
lessons.when: When a command is source-dev/admin, a source checkout is being maintained or an internal contract needs inspection.
lessons.need: Identify the contributor/operator audience and exact source-development authority before rendering, direct execution, schema operations or release maintenance.
lessons.surface: Source doctrine; generated agents/packets; dev/schema/scratch/source-authority and runner-fleet helpers
lessons.gap: These command families must be accounted for without presenting them as normal first-user prerequisites. Review question: which public stubs should route to the final contributor homes after reorganization?

lessons.title: Keep exact integration contracts discoverable without front-loading them
lessons.when: When authored integration data is rejected or a maintainer changes a schema/wire contract.
lessons.need: Find the canonical field/function/schema contract and its owner; temporal inputs, migrations and generated ownership are precise reference concerns, not new onboarding steps.
lessons.surface: Function/schema reference and newly added timestamp contract pages
lessons.gap: The two timestamp pages were added after the earlier public inventory. Review question: which parts belong in product API reference versus source architecture, and what refusal links reach them?
